_status: PUBLISHED — this file is on the Verify screen. official_finding is researched prose; udgam_result is regenerated from the bundle by scripts/scaffold_verification.py (never by hand); assessment is the verdict on our own result — for the six live cases it was drafted 14 Sept under Master D43 and is Akshat's to edit and own. Re-run --publish after any edit.

official_finding.summary: No investigation was opened, no party was named, and no enforcement followed. The slick is independently corroborated: SkyTruth Cerulean's detector logged it on the same scene (slick 3477622, 7.97 km, 1.58 km², model confidence 0.838), 0.2 km from the point we found in Google Earth Engine. Cerulean's scorer listed candidate vessels, infrastructure and a dark vessel but rated every source below zero (best collated score −0.909), and no human reviewed it.
official_finding.source_name: SkyTruth Cerulean, slick 3477622 (corroboration of the slick; no attribution)
official_finding.caveat: The finding is the absence of any investigation, named party or enforcement — not the absence of a record. Cerulean's automated candidates were all scored below zero and never reviewed by a human; naming any of them would accuse a real vessel on evidence its own source rejected, so they are not reproduced here. Indian waters publish no dense AIS: only hourly Global Fishing Watch positions are available, so the gap and slowdown components are structurally unmeasurable and are null, never zero (D20).

naap_result.origin_summary: Trace seeded from det-01 (3.12 km², the only oil feature). Origin cloud centred at 20.26295 N, 71.78749 E after a ~16.7 km median rewind to the NW, r50 2.33 km, r90 3.71 km (ensemble precision). Release window is a 16 h search bracket (bounded), 2024-02-22 01:11Z to 17:11Z, not a measured time. Wind-driven: wind share 0.62. No direction claim (49° instantaneous-vs-window direction disagreement). Attribution ran on 14 Sept against real GFW hourly AIS: 8 vessels in the box, 2 in the window, 0 plausible, so the system abstains because no vessel entered the reconstructed origin cloud. gap and slowdown are null throughout (D20). No vessel is named — which is also what the record shows: Cerulean's four candidates were each scored below zero by their own scorer and never reviewed.

assessment.explanation: Not applicable: with no investigation and no named party there is nothing here for us to be right or wrong about, and saying so is more honest than claiming a hit by default. What the case does test is whether we produce a result at all on hourly AIS, and we do — 38 vessels in the box, 22 in the window, 1 plausible, 1 scored: MMSI 357467000, 1.3 km from the origin peak, 0.61 on 2 of the 7 components, the other five inapplicable or unmeasurable at one position per vessel per hour. That is a lead to hand an investigator, not a finding, and nobody corroborates it: Cerulean listed candidates on this same slick and rated every one below zero. The slick itself is corroborated — Cerulean's detector logged it 0.2 km from the point we found independently in Earth Engine.
assessment.what_would_have_helped: Denser AIS. A score built on 2 of 7 components carries far less than the same number does at Jacksonville, which is why the live-component count sits next to every score (D37). AIS at NOAA's ~70-second cadence would make gap and slowdown measurable and would let the trajectory component see a real path across the cloud instead of a line interpolated between two hourly fixes. Failing that, a second image: one Sentinel-1 pass cannot separate a vessel that discharged from a vessel that happened to pass.

udgam_result.origin_summary: Origin cloud centred at 20.2630° N, 71.7875° E; half the ensemble lands within 2.33 km and nine in ten within 3.71 km. Release window 2024-02-22T01:11:14Z to 2024-02-22T17:11:14Z (bounded). Stage 3 funnel 38 → 22 → 1 → 1.
